problem.paragraph: 9. Details A rectangular plane and a wave are graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The plane is warped such that the longer sides of the plane, parallel to the x axis, are in the shape of a wave traveling parallel to the x axis. The vertical trace of the wavy plane on the x z plane traces a wave such that a peak of the wave crosses the positive z axis. $$z = \cos x$$

10. Details A rectangular plane and a curve are graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The plane is bent such that it traces a curve on the y z plane. The curve enters from the top right, goes down steeply to the left, concave up, approaches the x axis and crosses it at the origin, goes down steeply to the left, and concave down.

list.item: Find and identify the traces of the quadric surface $$x^{2} + y^{2} - z^{2} = 1$$ and explain why the graph looks like the graph of the hyperboloid of one sheet in Table 1.
If we change the equation in part (a) to $$x^{2} - y^{2} + z^{2} = 1$$ , how is the graph affected?
What if we change the equation in part (a) to $$x^{2} + y^{2} + 2y - z^{2} = 0$$ ?

solution.paragraph: The hyperboloid is rotated so that its axis is the $$y$$ -axis.
The hyperboloid is shifted one unit in the negative $$y$$ -direction.

image.alt: Details Three almost concentric parabolas are graphed on the y z coordinate plane. The y axis is horizontal and the z axis is vertical. All three parabolas open leftward. The first parabola is labeled k = plus minus 2 and has its vertex at the origin. The second parabola is labeled k = plus minus 1 and has its vertex on the positive y axis. The third parabola is labeled k = 0 and has its vertex on the positive y axis, close to and to the right of the second parabola. The arms of the second and third parabola converge slightly more than the parabola immediately to the left.

Details Three concentric circles are graphed on the x z coordinate plane. The x axis is horizontal and the z axis is vertical. The circles have their center at the origin. A point at the origin is labeled k = 1. The innermost circle is labeled k = 0. The middle circle is labeled k = negative 1. The outermost circle is labeled k = negative 2.

Details Three concentric ellipses are graphed on the y z coordinate plane. The y axis is horizontal and the z axis is vertical. The ellipses have their center at the origin and are symmetric about both the x and y axes. Their vertical width is more than their horizontal width. The innermost ellipse is labeled k = 0. The middle ellipse is close to the innermost one and is labeled k = plus minus 1. The outermost ellipse is a bit further from the middle ellipse and is labeled k = plus minus 2.

Details Three hyperbolas are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The first hyperbola is labeled k = 0, has its vertices on the positive and negative y axes with its arms wide. The second hyperbola is labeled k = 1 and is composed of two lines intersecting at the origin. The third hyperbola is labeled k = 2 and has its vertices on the negative and positive x axis with its arm opening much narrower than k = 0.

problem.paragraph: Sketch the region bounded by the surfaces $$z = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}$$ and $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$$ for $$1 \leqslant z \leqslant 2$$ .
Sketch the region bounded by the paraboloids $$z = x^{2} + y^{2}$$ and $$z = 2 - x^{2} - y^{2}$$ .
Find an equation for the surface obtained by rotating the curve $$y = \sqrt{x}$$ about the $$x$$ -axis.
Find an equation for the surface obtained by rotating the line $$z = 2y$$ about the $$z$$ -axis.
Find an equation for the surface consisting of all points that are equidistant from the point $$\left( {- 1,0,0} \right)$$ and the plane $$x = 1$$ . Identify the surface.

Find an equation for the surface consisting of all points $$P$$ for which the distance from $$P$$ to the $$x$$ -axis is twice the distance from $$P$$ to the $$\mathit{yz}$$ -plane. Identify the surface.

Traditionally, the earth’s surface has been modeled as a sphere, but the World Geodetic System of 1984 (WGS-84) uses an ellipsoid as a more accurate model. It places the center of the earth at the origin and the north pole on the positive $$z$$ -axis. The distance from the center to the poles is $$6356.523$$ km and the distance to a point on the equator is $$6378.137$$ km.

list.item: Find an equation of the earth’s surface as used by WGS-84.
Curves of equal latitude are traces in the planes $$z = k$$ . What is the shape of these curves?
Meridians (curves of equal longitude) are traces in planes of the form $$y = mx$$ . What is the shape of these meridians?

problem.paragraph: A cooling tower for a nuclear reactor is to be constructed in the shape of a hyperboloid of one sheet [see Figure 12(b)]. The diameter at the base is $$280$$ m and the minimum diameter, $$500$$ m above the base, is $$200$$ m. Find an equation for the tower.

Show that if the point $$\left( {a,b,c} \right)$$ lies on the hyperbolic paraboloid $$z = y^{2} - x^{2}$$ , then the lines with parametric equations $$x = a + t$$ , $$y = b + t$$ , $$z = c + 2\left( {b - a} \right)t$$ and $$x = a + t$$ , $$y = b - t$$ , $$z = c - 2\left( {b + a} \right)t$$ both lie entirely on this paraboloid. (This shows that the hyperbolic paraboloid is what is called a ruled surface; that is, it can be generated by the motion of a straight line. In fact, this exercise shows that through each point on the hyperbolic paraboloid there are two generating lines. The only other quadric surfaces that are ruled surfaces are cylinders, cones, and hyperboloids of one sheet.)
Show that the curve of intersection of the surfaces $$x^{2} + 2y^{2} - z^{2} + 3x = 1$$ and $$2x^{2} + 4y^{2} - 2z^{2} - 5y = 0$$ lies in a plane.

Graph the surfaces $$z = x^{2} + y^{2}$$ and $$z = 1 - y^{2}$$ on a common screen using the domain $$|x| \leqslant 1.2$$ , $$|y| \leqslant 1.2$$ and observe the curve of intersection of these surfaces. Show that the projection of this curve onto the $$\mathit{xy}$$ -plane is an ellipse.
